item.title: KRAS<sup>G12D</sup>-targeted therapy sensitivity depends on interferon signaling activation in pancreatic cancer.
item.author: Zhang Y, Tang S, Zhang Y, Liu J, Shi X, Li Y, Li Y, Wang H, Zhong C, Sun M, Li W, Zhu Y, Yang W, Zhao Y, Guo S, Wu Z, Wang L, Jin G, Gao D.
item.description:
KRAS G12D is a predominant driver in pancreatic cancer, yet the basis of intrinsic resistance to KRAS G12D -targeted therapy remains poorly defined. Integrated genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics profiling across 242 patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and matched tumor tissues reveals a KRAS G12D -mutant subset intrinsically resistant to KRAS G12D -targeted therapeutics, characterized by marked downregulation of innate immune signaling pathways. Functional validation demonstrates that suppressing interferon signaling in sensitive models induces resistance, whereas activation of interferon signaling, particularly interferon beta (IFN-β), increases sensitivity in resistant models. Combining IFN-β with KRAS inhibitors (MRTX1133, HRS-4642, and RMC-6236) exhibits synergistic antitumor effects in intrinsically resistant pancreatic cancer. item.title: A sex-specific platelet switch controls anti-tumor immunity in glioblastoma.
item.author: Sloan AR, Bukenya G, Tannish GP, Silver DJ, Aggarwal A, Lee J, Rosoff D, Alban TJ, Juric I, Parsai S, Baruah V, Bodovetz T, Whitfield D, Tack L, Navadgi T, Reitz N, Ho ST, Badani A, Goldberg J, Yuan X, Gaboriau A, Kamatala S, Coker J, Kumar VS, Jain SS, Xu C, Scalise A, Rajasekar B, Vincenti A, Mulkearns-Hubert EE, Horbinski CM, Sloan AE, Hubert CG, Luo J, Rubin JB, Stavrou EX, Lohoff FW, Goodman WA, Miller TE, O'Connor CM, Nieman MT, Sangwan N, Chan TA, Khorana AA, Dhawan A, Cameron SJ, Lathia JD.
item.description:
Sex differences in glioblastoma (GBM) outcomes are shaped by biological, hormonal, and immune factors, but the mechanisms driving these disparities remain unclear. We identify platelet protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) signaling as a regulator of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity. GBM patients exhibit increased platelet reactivity driven by PAR4. In murine models, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PAR4 prolongs survival in females, but not males, and is estrogen dependent, persisting in hormonal females regardless of chromosomal sex. The survival advantage is mediated within the tumor microenvironment through enhanced CD8 + T cell infiltration and function. PAR4-activated platelets suppress CD8 + T cell activity, whereas CD8 + T cell depletion abolishes both tumor-induced platelet reactivity and the PAR4-dependent survival advantage. item.title: Intrinsic resistance to KRAS inhibition: Interfering with interferon.
item.author: Miguel-López B, Drosten M.
item.description:
In this issue of Cancer Cell, Zhang et al. perform multi-omics profiling on a large collection of patient-derived pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma organoids to elucidate the mechanisms underlying intrinsic resistance to KRAS inhibition. This work identifies suppression of innate immune signaling through sustained MYC activity as the principal driver of intrinsic resistance.

item.title: CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore predict individual outcomes but not trial results after neoadjuvant therapy for early breast cancer.
item.author: Conforti F, Nekljudova V, Holtschmidt J, Sala I, Pagan E, Solbach C, Untch M, Denkert C, Bagnardi V, Bendoni M, Fasching PA, Schneeweiss A, Lück HJ, Valenza C, Viale G, De Pas T, van Mackelenbergh M, Huober J, Müller V, Link T, Karn T, Reinisch M, Marmé F, Bjelic-Radisic V, Schem C, Hartkopf A, Stickeler E, Hanusch C, Blohmer JU, Fehm T, Rhiem K, Gelber RD, Loibl S.
item.description:
CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore are prognostic scores estimating the risk of recurrence after neoadjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer, but can they predict the long-term outcomes in a clinical trial? In this study, we assessed their surrogacy values at patient level and trial level for long-term outcomes, using data from 8,359 patients across nine neoadjuvant randomized trials conducted by the German Breast Group (GBG) and AGO-B study group. We found that at the patient level, both scores were significantly associated with outcomes, but at the trial level, the associations with distant disease-free survival (DDFS), invasive disease-free survival (iDFS), and overall survival (OS) were weak for both scores (R 2 range = 0.03 to 0.24, with wide confidence intervals). item.title: Antibiotics and outcomes of cancer immunotherapy: An updated meta-analysis and clinical applications.
item.author: Porcari S, Bolte LA, Björk JR, Elkrief A, Derosa L, Ferrari M, Pezzullo AM, Severino A, Fusco W, Messaoudene M, Costa Silva CA, Fidelle M, Routy B, Mählmann L, Thomas AM, Ciccarese C, Nero C, Fagotti A, Tortora G, Gasbarrini A, Iacovelli R, Bria E, Futreal A, McQuade J, Kroemer G, Hospers GAP, de Haan JJ, Wargo J, Segata N, Weersma RK, Ianiro G, Zitvogel L, Seerave Global Oncobiome Network.
item.description:
The gut microbiome is a modifiable determinant of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), positioning antibiotic exposure as a critical yet under-recognized risk factor for worse survival outcomes in immuno-oncology. As nearly 30% of ICI-treated patients receive antibiotics and indications of cancer immunotherapy are expanding, this issue represents a global challenge in oncology. Here, we paint an updated and comprehensive landscape of antibiotic exposure in immuno-oncology, provide actionable clinical recommendations, and envision future avenues for improvement. First, we describe the biological mechanisms by which antibiotic-induced dysbiosis contributes to ICI resistance. item.title: Macrophage lipid signaling drives glioblastoma invasion and represents a therapeutic vulnerability.
item.author: Pallarés-Moratalla C, Guyot M, Gopalan KS, Robl B, Idkowiak J, Dehairs J, Ravoet N, Hendriks TFE, Nowak KA, Lakić ND, Weng L, Konstantakos V, Spotbeen X, Serneels L, Fendt SM, Aerts S, De Smet F, Cuypers E, Swinnen JV, Bergers G.
item.description:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by diffuse infiltration into the surrounding brain, limiting complete surgical resection, the strongest determinant of patient survival. The mechanisms driving this invasive growth remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a lipid-mediated paracrine signaling axis through which tumor-associated microglia/macrophages promote glioma invasion. Integrating single-cell transcriptomics, spatial lipidomics, and functional perturbation across mouse models and human GBM samples, we show that invading tumor cells engage and reprogram myeloid cells via colony-stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF1R)-PI3K signaling. This induces lipid metabolic reprogramming and secretion of bioactive lipids, including lysophosphatidylcholines (LPCs) and lysophosphatidic acids (LPAs), which promote GBM invasion through distinct downstream pathways. item.title: Finding MES: A hidden cell state in neuroblastoma.
item.author: Hayes MN, Irwin MS.
item.description:
In this issue of Cancer Cell, Patel et al. integrate bulk and single-cell/single-nucleus RNA sequencing with spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics across neuroblastoma patient-derived xenografts and annotated tumors to reveal adrenergic and mesenchymal signatures, identify distinct tumor cell populations in vivo, and demonstrate associations with patient outcomes.

item.title: Lung neuroendocrine cancer induces immunosuppressive macrophages via serotonin to drive resistance to the T cell engager tarlatamab.
item.author: Nomura K, Fukami T, Kato S, Tanaka S, Fukuda A, Koike Y, Kondo M, Kumagai K, Irie T, Okumura G, Taki T, Sakashita S, Shirasawa M, Yoshida T, Shiraishi K, Ariyasu R, Takeyasu Y, Niimi T, Sakai T, Torasawa M, Kanemura H, Saito S, Hayashi T, Kanai A, Takamochi K, Haruki T, Aokage K, Nishinakamura H, Koyama S, Ishii G, Suzuki Y, Goto Y, Nishio M, Suzuki K, Tsutani Y, Yatabe Y, Mano H, Tsuboi M, Kumagai S, Nishikawa H.
item.description:
Tarlatamab, a delta-like protein 3 (DLL3) × CD3-directed T cell engager (TCE), provides clinical efficacy against small cell lung cancers (SCLCs), although its efficacy remains limited, indicating the importance of clarifying the resistance mechanisms. We show that serotonin (5-HT) produced by DLL3 high neuroendocrine cancers (NECs) induces immunosuppressive tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), resulting in impaired CD8 + T cell function and TCE resistance. Using SCLC and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma cohorts, we find that DLL3 high SCLCs induce immunosuppressive TAMs in the tumor microenvironment and become resistant to tarlatamab. DLL3 high NECs increase 5-HT production via TPH1 upregulation. item.title: How far are we from multi-omics states to therapeutic targets in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer?
item.author: Chen YX, Chen J, Wang F.
item.description:
In this issue of Cancer Cell, Sadanandam et al. integrate multi-omics profiling of microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer with patient-derived models, identifying focal adhesion kinase and phosphoinositide-dependent kinase 1 as promising therapeutic targets. The study advances multi-omics discoveries toward functional precision oncology and potential treatment strategies to guide clinical translation.

item.title: Multiomic characterization of microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer reveals distinct biology and targetable vulnerabilities.

item.description:
Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) is a molecularly complex and clinically challenging disease subtype, lacking effective targeted therapies. Leveraging multiomic data from ∼2,000 tumor samples (including 316MSS CRCs not previously profiled) representing ∼4,500 molecular profiles and 195,246 single cells/nuclei, we uncover complex biology and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Application of a multiomic-phenomic integrative framework, including iPhenMap (a machine-learning tool), reveals complex molecular programs, including replication stress, right-sided biology, glutaminolysis-driven metabolic reprogramming, and MYC-E2F transcriptional networks governing epigenetic remodeling and perineural invasion.
